children: US household inflation expectations rose in October while consumer sentiment barely changed. The readings add context ahead of the Federal Reserve’s October 27–28 meeting, without establishing a rate decision or a Bitcoin price direction.

American households expect prices to rise faster over both the next year and the longer run, according to the University of Michigan’s final October survey. For Bitcoin traders heading into another Federal Reserve decision, the release adds an inflation concern to an already important policy week.

The university’s October 23 results put year-ahead inflation expectations at 4.7%, up from 4.6% in September. Long-run expectations increased from 3.4% to 3.5%. Both measures rose for a second consecutive month and reached their highest readings since May.

Consumer sentiment was almost unchanged at 48.0, compared with 48.1 in September. Beneath that steady headline, the current-conditions index fell to 46.7 while the expectations index improved to 48.8. The university linked weaker conditions for buying durable goods to affordability concerns and higher interest rates.
A policy meeting with competing pressures

The Fed’s published calendar places its next meeting on October 27–28. Its most recent decision, on September 16, raised the federal funds target by a quarter of a percentage point to 3.75%–4.00%. That statement described inflation as elevated and reaffirmed the central bank’s 2% objective.

Michigan’s figures measure what households expect. They are separate from actual consumer-price inflation and from the Fed’s own projections. Comparing the survey’s percentages directly with the policy target would overlook differences in the measure and the time horizon.

The distinction does not make expectations irrelevant. In an earlier Fed explanation of the subject, then-Governor Adriana Kugler described longer-term expectations as a useful indication of monetary-policy credibility because they tend to respond less to short-lived price shocks.
The implication for crypto depends on the response

One plausible reading is that rising expectations make it harder for policymakers to sound comfortable about inflation. The weaker assessment of current conditions creates a competing concern: households are already feeling the effects of expensive credit and reduced purchasing power. Neither signal determines the committee’s decision by itself.

For Bitcoin and Ethereum, the transmission runs through financing conditions, the return available on cash and investors’ willingness to hold volatile assets. Higher expected inflation can strengthen the appeal of scarce assets in principle, while tighter monetary policy can work against speculative demand. Treating the survey as an automatic bullish or bearish signal misses that tension.
Dollar stablecoins illustrate another distinction: maintaining a dollar peg does not protect a holder from changes in that dollar’s purchasing power.

The immediate checkpoint is Wednesday’s policy announcement. Traders will have to judge the decision alongside the Fed’s explanation of inflation and growth, rather than infer an entire rate path from one household survey.
Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Bitcoin’s Fed Week Starts With A Fresh Rise In US Inflation Expectations
